Artifact: litellm-1.107.0.tar.gz (source distribution)

The archive contains 4,709 regular files. Its pyproject.toml declares
tool.maturin.data = "cook", but the archive contains no cook/ directory,
.pth file, sitecustomize.py or usercustomize.py. The Rust build.rs only
adds macOS linker arguments. No wheel credential stealer or remote loader
is present in this source archive. The injected data setting remains an
incident indicator; it does not prove payload execution in these bytes.

The October incident is not attributed to TeamPCP. October markers move
to well-known/malware/stealer/privcollect. Their descriptions and severities
now distinguish indicator co-occurrence from collection, exfiltration and
startup execution. Generic objective rules assess actual decoded payload
operations independently. No external consumers referenced the relocated
October IDs or the renamed Maturin data-directory property.

Maturin's data setting selects a wheel data directory; its subdirectories
select install schemes. It does not alone prove purelib installation.
The cook spelling is a campaign indicator, so it belongs with that incident,
not as a suspicious generic build property. No replacement hostile rule
is invented for the payload-free source archive. Training ruling: bad, per
the user's classification of this tampered release artifact. The absence of
the wheel payload does not change that training label.
